Plain Sight
Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date}

Good morning. Three bits of news and one worked example. The consultation on the public sector accessibility guidance closes on Friday 30 October, so if you have views, this is the week.

News

Guidance consultation closes 30 October

The draft update to the public sector guidance adds a section on documents and PDFs, and finally says something about video captions on social media. The response form takes about 20 minutes.

Read →

Screen reader survey results

This year's survey of 1,800 screen reader users found that headings are still the most used way to move around a page, by a long way. Landmarks came third, behind search.

Read →

A free audit for charities

A group of auditors is offering 40 small charities a free review of their donate page. Applications open until the end of November.

Read →

Worked example

Disclosure buttons that say what they do

A reader sent us an FAQ page where each question opened its answer on click. It looked fine and was silent to a screen reader: the questions were headings with a click handler, so there was nothing to focus and nothing announced when the answer appeared.

The fix is a real button inside the heading, with its state on it:

<h3>
  <button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-3">
    Can I change my delivery date?
  </button>
</h3>
<div id="faq-3" hidden>...</div>

Toggle aria-expanded and the hidden attribute together. Now the question is in the tab order, it's announced as a collapsed button, and the heading still shows up in the headings list. No icon text needed: the expanded state does the job the plus sign was doing.

Ruth

Have a page you'd like us to look at? Reply to this email. We pick one each issue and always ask before naming anyone.

issues.text:
PLAIN SIGHT Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date} View in your browser: https://plainsight.example/issues/plain-sight-error-messages-a-screen-reader-will-read Good morning. A worked example about forms this week, because we keep seeing the same mistake. NEWS New guidance on cognitive accessibility A working group has published plain-language guidance on making services easier for people with memory and attention difficulties. It is short and readable, which is a good sign. Read: https://plainsight.example/l/new-guidance-on-cognitive-accessibility A captioning service closes A volunteer captioning project for local council meetings is closing after six years. Its founders have published what they learned. Read: https://plainsight.example/l/a-captioning-service-closes Accessibility statements, checked Researchers checked 500 public sector accessibility statements. A third hadn't been updated in over two years. Read: https://plainsight.example/l/accessibility-statements-checked WORKED EXAMPLE Error messages a screen reader will read This week's example is a sign-up form where errors appeared in red under each field after submitting. Sighted users saw them. Screen reader users heard nothing, and focus stayed on the submit button. Three changes fixed it. Link each message to its field, mark the field invalid, and move focus to an error summary at the top:

Enter an email address like name@example.com

The summary lists each error as a link to its field. Users hear how many problems there are, and can jump straight to each one. Note the message itself: it says what to do, not just that something is wrong. Ruth -- Plain Sight is written by Ruth Abara. Plain Sight CIC, 15 Marlowe Road, Brighton BN2 3HD. Plain Sight
Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date}

Good morning. A worked example about forms this week, because we keep seeing the same mistake.

News

New guidance on cognitive accessibility

A working group has published plain-language guidance on making services easier for people with memory and attention difficulties. It is short and readable, which is a good sign.

Read →

A captioning service closes

A volunteer captioning project for local council meetings is closing after six years. Its founders have published what they learned.

Read →

Accessibility statements, checked

Researchers checked 500 public sector accessibility statements. A third hadn't been updated in over two years.

Read →

Worked example

Error messages a screen reader will read

This week's example is a sign-up form where errors appeared in red under each field after submitting. Sighted users saw them. Screen reader users heard nothing, and focus stayed on the submit button.

Three changes fixed it. Link each message to its field, mark the field invalid, and move focus to an error summary at the top:

<input id="email" aria-invalid="true"
  aria-describedby="email-error">
<p id="email-error">Enter an email address
  like name@example.com</p>

The summary lists each error as a link to its field. Users hear how many problems there are, and can jump straight to each one. Note the message itself: it says what to do, not just that something is wrong.

Ruth

issues.subject: Plain Sight: focus after a dialog closes
issues.text:
PLAIN SIGHT
Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date}

View in your browser: https://plainsight.example/issues/plain-sight-focus-after-a-dialog-closes

Good morning. Dialogs this week. They're everywhere, and almost every one we test loses the user's place when it closes.

NEWS

A new colour contrast tool for designers
It checks a whole palette at once and suggests the nearest passing shade. Free, works offline.

Read: https://plainsight.example/l/a-new-colour-contrast-tool-for-designers

Court case on an inaccessible booking site
A cinema chain has settled with a blind customer who couldn't book seats. The settlement includes an audit and a fix within a year.

Read: https://plainsight.example/l/court-case-on-an-inaccessible-booking-site

Captions in video calls
Researchers compared automatic captions across four calling apps for speakers with regional accents. Accuracy varied from 71% to 93%.

Read: https://plainsight.example/l/captions-in-video-calls

WORKED EXAMPLE

Focus after a dialog closes
A reader's settings page opened a 'Delete account' dialog. When it closed, focus went to the top of the page. A keyboard user had to tab through forty links to get back to where they were.

The rule: when a dialog closes, focus goes back to the control that opened it. If you're using the native dialog element, much of this is handled for you:

    const opener = document.activeElement;
    dialog.showModal();
    dialog.addEventListener("close", () => opener.focus());

If the opener no longer exists (say the user deleted the item it belonged to), move focus to the nearest sensible place, such as the list it was in, and say what happened.

Ruth

--
Plain Sight is written by Ruth Abara. Plain Sight CIC, 15 Marlowe Road, Brighton BN2 3HD. Community interest company no. 12870455.

issues.text:
PLAIN SIGHT Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date} View in your browser: https://plainsight.example/issues/plain-sight-tables-that-make-sense-out-loud Good morning. Data tables this week, because a reader's bank statement page was read to them as one long string of numbers. NEWS Large print by default A national charity has moved its printed letters to 16 point by default. Complaints about the cost of extra pages: two. Read: https://plainsight.example/l/large-print-by-default Alt text in social posts A study of 10,000 posts from public bodies found that 18% of images had alt text. Many of those just said 'image'. Read: https://plainsight.example/l/alt-text-in-social-posts Free training for content designers Six one-hour sessions on writing accessible content, recorded and free to watch. Read: https://plainsight.example/l/free-training-for-content-designers WORKED EXAMPLE Tables that make sense out loud The statement page used a grid of divs styled to look like a table. Visually clear; to a screen reader, just a run of dates and amounts with no way to know which column was which. A real table with header cells fixes it, because screen readers announce the header as you move between cells: ...
Transactions, October
Date Description Amount
The caption names the table so it can be found in a list of tables. If you need a table to scroll sideways on small screens, wrap it in a region with a label and make the region focusable, so keyboard users can scroll it too. Ruth -- Plain Sight is written by Ruth Abara. Plain Sight CIC, 15 Marlowe Road, Brighton BN2 3HD. Community interest company no. 12870455. Plain Sight
Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date}

Good morning. Data tables this week, because a reader's bank statement page was read to them as one long string of numbers.

News

Large print by default

A national charity has moved its printed letters to 16 point by default. Complaints about the cost of extra pages: two.

Read →

Alt text in social posts

A study of 10,000 posts from public bodies found that 18% of images had alt text. Many of those just said 'image'.

Read →

Free training for content designers

Six one-hour sessions on writing accessible content, recorded and free to watch.

Read →

Worked example

Tables that make sense out loud

The statement page used a grid of divs styled to look like a table. Visually clear; to a screen reader, just a run of dates and amounts with no way to know which column was which.

A real table with header cells fixes it, because screen readers announce the header as you move between cells:

<table>
  <caption>Transactions, October</caption>
  <tr><th scope="col">Date</th>
      <th scope="col">Description</th>
      <th scope="col">Amount</th></tr>
  ...
</table>

The caption names the table so it can be found in a list of tables. If you need a table to scroll sideways on small screens, wrap it in a region with a label and make the region focusable, so keyboard users can scroll it too.

Ruth

Plain Sight is written by Ruth Abara. Plain Sight CIC, 15 Marlowe Road, Brighton BN2 3HD. Community interest company no. 12870455.

Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date}

Good morning. Short issue this week. Link text is the example, and it's an old one, but we found it on three new sites last week alone.

News

Accessibility in procurement

A large city council now scores accessibility as 20% of every digital contract. Suppliers have to show an audit, not a promise.

Read →

Easy read versions, compared

A charity tested easy read leaflets with 60 people with learning disabilities. Pictures helped only when they showed the actual thing, not a symbol.

Read →

Keyboard shortcuts that clash

A useful list of single-key shortcuts in web apps that conflict with screen reader commands, and how to avoid them.

Read →

Worked example

Links that make sense on their own

Screen reader users often pull up a list of all the links on a page. On a reader's news site, that list was 'Read more' fourteen times.

The best fix is to make the headline the link and drop 'Read more' altogether. If the design needs the extra link, give it the headline as its accessible name:

<a href="/news/library-hours"
  aria-describedby="h-library-hours">Read more</a>

Better still, write link text that describes where it goes: 'Library opening hours for the holidays' works for everyone, not only screen reader users.

Ruth

issues.subject: Plain Sight: motion that respects the setting
issues.text:
PLAIN SIGHT
Accessibility news and one worked example. Monday {date}

View in your browser: https://plainsight.example/issues/plain-sight-motion-that-respects-the-setting

Good morning. Animation this week. We like motion that helps, and we like it more when it switches off for people who've asked it to.

NEWS

Vestibular disorders and the web
A charity has published first-hand accounts from people who get dizzy or sick from parallax and large animations. Required reading for anyone who designs motion.

Read: https://plainsight.example/l/vestibular-disorders-and-the-web

A shared component library goes public
A group of universities has released its accessible component library, tested with disabled students.

Read: https://plainsight.example/l/a-shared-component-library-goes-public

PDF forms, still
A survey found that 40% of council application forms are still PDFs that can't be filled in with a screen reader.

Read: https://plainsight.example/l/pdf-forms-still

WORKED EXAMPLE

Motion that respects the setting
A reader's landing page had cards that slid and scaled as you scrolled. With reduced motion turned on in their system settings, nothing changed.

Wrap the movement in a media query, and keep a gentle fade so the change is still visible:

    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .card { transition: opacity 0.2s; transform: none; }
    }

Don't remove every transition: an instant change can be harder to follow than a short fade. The aim is no large movement across the screen, not no feedback at all.

Ruth

--
Plain Sight is written by Ruth Abara. Plain Sight CIC, 15 Marlowe Road, Brighton BN2 3HD. Community interest company no. 12870455.
